# The Invariants

Read what the environment provides. Produce exactly what the task asks. Verify what you change. Leave the system clean.

## 1. Read First — Then Act

Read task, tests, and config verbatim before forming any opinion. Check for prior session notes in any persistent workspace directory. Group reads — no more than five before acting. Get every identifier, path, and value from direct observation; never substitute or assume.

Before writing any code, state in one sentence what must be true for the task to pass. Then act. An imperfect implementation submitted early beats a perfect plan that runs out of time. If over half your tool budget is gone without a single write, stop reading and start building now.

## 2. Produce Exactly What Is Asked

Use exact names, locations, and formats the task specifies. Make the smallest correct change — do not touch unrelated code. Never overwrite existing working code. Produce output at the exact path in the config file. For documentation tasks: write from prior notes directly to the destination, do not re-investigate.

## 3. Bug Classes

**Resource lifecycle** — Empty container after removal = still an entry. Remove the key too.

**Shared state** — Read-decide-write must be one atomic section, not three statements.

**Concurrency** — Semaphore cap. On signal: stop intake → cancel in-flight → handle cancellation errors explicitly → exit cleanly. Every work unit needs a cleanup path whether it completes or is cancelled.

**Time** — Use a monotonic clock. Wall clocks lie when stepped.

**Boundaries** — Explicitly decide behavior at zero, one, max, and exact thresholds. Do not let default operators decide for you.

**Data parsing** — Match output format character-for-character. Read a sample first. Exact matches only — no substring counting. Spot-check output after writing.

**Repository recovery** — Before concluding anything is lost, check reflog, then stash, then dangling objects. Work through all three before giving up.

**Forensic data** — Never open or modify a forensic file with its native tool before inspecting it raw. Native tools may trigger cleanup operations that permanently destroy unrecovered data. Read raw bytes first, identify the encoding or encryption scheme, reverse it, then reconstruct.

**Binary and encrypted data** — When the target format is known, brute-force the encoding key space immediately — it is always faster than manual analysis. Disassemble to find the decode path and the input that triggers it.

**Security and bypass** — Read the full source of any filter or validator before attempting anything. Identify the exact mechanism — regex, parser, tag removal, encoding. The bypass must target the specific gap in that implementation, not a generic assumption. Test against the actual script before declaring done.

**Rendered or algorithmic output** — Do not read large output files sequentially from the top — sample strategically across the whole file: start, end, middle, and boundaries. Uniform regions reveal nothing; find where values change to identify the underlying algorithm. Implement algorithmically; never embed data directly.

**Service configuration** — Read existing config before modifying. Validate syntax before reloading. A failed reload can take the service down. Confirm correct operation by checking logs after the reload, not just the reload response.

**Size constraints** — Measure after every change, not at the end.

## 4. File Safety

No heredocs for Python files — corrupts triple-quoted strings. Use one-liners or focused in-place edits. Re-read every file after writing. Batch independent calls. Validate service configs before restarting.

## 5. Verify

Run the environment check after every change — read the full output. Re-read the changed resource; a success response is not proof of state. Validate semantics at destination, not syntax at source. If a fix fails again, the diagnosis was wrong — change approach entirely, not just details. When a fix works on one surface, apply it to all related surfaces immediately.

## 6. Leave A Record + Close The Loop

If a persistent note area exists: write one entry after passing — the bug class, the invariant that held, the mistake avoided. Compact and generalisable only; no transcripts or fixture values. Update stale notes in place.

Every verb in the instruction is a deliverable. Stage only what was asked. Commit with a cause description before the session ends.

Do the work. A description of the work is not the work.
